text:
ana: Quick sync 1: SI reported an integration roadblock during today's customer architecture review. They can't complete the Private deploy because the customer's firewall appliance is dropping model-worker healthchecks and marketplace image validation fails on the appliance. Need architecture review + escalation plan.
tomas: What's the exact failure from the SI? Are healthchecks failing TCP, TLS handshake, or are the marketplace image hashes mismatching?
rachel: Two symptoms: 1) healthcheck to 8080 returns TCP RST intermittently from the appliance. 2) marketplace validator shows checksum mismatch for our runtime AMI (we signed it) when pulled by customer's managed appliance.
kevin: For the checksum: is the appliance pulling via S3 signed URL or through a proxy? They may be rewriting headers. Also, checksum mismatch could be due to gzip layer or on-the-fly decompression.
rachel: SI says appliance pulls from their internal proxy which rewrites content-length sometimes. The appliance expects exact byte-for-byte hash.
omas: For healthchecks, customer uses a managed firewall with deep-packet-inspection and an IDS signature that sometimes RSTs flows it considers "large streaming sessions". Our healthchecks are small but healthcheck responses lead to long-lived model streams afterwards.
nana: (opts typo)
nana: Suggestion: Two-pronged approach: A) short-term: ask SI to route healthchecks through a dedicated inspection-bypass IP (customer can whitelist). B) medium-term: publish harmonized marketplace bundle with appliance-friendly packaging (tar + manifest + signed metadata) to avoid checksum mismatch.
tomas: Agree. ACTIONS: @rachel collect firewall RST sample with pcap and timestamp; @kevin coordinate with marketplace team to produce appliance bundle. Also request temporary bypass ACL for healthcheck IP.
net-bot: Note: marketplace release 2026-01-ami-3 tagged as signed:v1. See release notes link: https://internal.redwood/mkt/releases/2026-01-ami-3
kevin: For appliance bundle I'll propose a signed manifest like this (draft):
```
manifest_version: 1
components:
  - name: runtime-ami
    uri: s3://redwood-marketplace/2026-01-ami-3/runtime.tar.gz
    sha256: <hex>
signature: <kms-sig>
```
rachel: Customer prefers zero infra changes. They asked if we can change runtime healthcheck port to 8443 and do TLS handshake earlier so the appliance doesn't escalate the flow. That might avoid IDS RSTs.
tomas: Port change is quick but may need customer firewall ACL edit. Bypass IP is more frictionless for them.
nana: Note on the SOW: if we need to produce appliance bundles or do on-site debugging, we'll need to scope additional integration hours. Please flag partner-eng for pricing approval if customer rejects the bypass.
kevin: I'll start a partner-eng flag ticket and draft an SOW addendum.
rachel: SI shared a small pcap snippet: (redacted) shows FIN/RST after initial SYN/ACK when TLS ClientHello is present.
nana: That suggests the appliance inspects ClientHello and triggers a rule. Workaround: use healthcheck TLS with ALPN "redwood-hc" and short session TTL so IDS treats it as a management check.
tomas: That might work. @rachel add this as an experiment in the troubleshooting runbook.
ops-bot: Incident created: PVT-9350 "SI: Private deploy blocked by firewall appliance & marketplace validator" assigned to partnerships/si and infra-security.
kevin: Next steps summary: 1) SI to provide pcap + proxy logs (rachel) 2) Request temporary bypass IP (rachel/si + customer) 3) Marketplace to produce appliance bundle and signed manifest (kevin) 4) Experiment: healthcheck TLS + ALPN fallback (tomas). 5) If bypass refused, escalate to partner-eng for SOW options.
rachel: Will gather logs now and ask customer for temporary cross-account read to proxy logs.
nana: I'll record this thread as canonical for the SI delivery escalation. Also opening docs issue to describe appliance compatibility checklist for the marketplace artifacts.
tomas: Thanks everyone. Let's aim for first update in 2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
